Coffee Ratio Calculator

For drip or pour over, use 1 g of coffee for every 16 g of water: 15 g (about 3 level tablespoons) for a 240 ml cup. French press is stronger at 1:14.

—

Coffee ratios by brew method

Coffee to water by weight
MethodRatioPer cup
Drip / pour over1:1615 g per 240 ml cup
French press1:1417 g per 240 ml cup
Cold brew (concentrate)1:830 g per 240 ml, then dilute 1:1
Espresso1:218 g coffee → 36 g espresso

1 ml of water weighs 1 g, so the water in grams and in milliliters is the same number. Tablespoon amounts assume about 5 g per level tablespoon of ground coffee, and are approximate.

How it works

A ratio like 1:16 means 1 gram of coffee for every 16 grams of water. The calculator multiplies your cups by the cup size to get the water, then divides by the ratio to get the coffee. For espresso it works per shot instead: an 18 g dose pulled to about 36 g of espresso. It all runs in your browser. Nothing you type is sent anywhere or saved.

Start with the ratio in the table, then adjust to taste: less water (1:15) for stronger coffee, more (1:17) for lighter. Change one thing at a time.

Ways to use it

  • Morning pour over. Weigh 15 to 30 g and you’re done thinking about it.
  • French press for guests. Scale up to a full pot without guessing scoops.
  • Cold brew concentrate. A big batch at 1:8, diluted when you pour it.
  • A new bag of beans. Start from the standard ratio and adjust from there.

Questions

What ratio should I start with?

1:16 for drip and pour over, 1:14 for French press, 1:8 for cold brew concentrate and 1:2 for espresso. Then adjust a little at a time to taste.

Why grams instead of scoops?

A scoop of coarse coffee and a scoop of fine coffee weigh different amounts, and scoops come in different sizes. Grams are the same every time, so the coffee tastes the same every time.

How strong is cold brew concentrate?

At 1:8 it’s about twice as strong as regular coffee. Mix it 1:1 with water or milk when you serve it, or a bit less if you like it strong.

Can I use tablespoons?

Yes, roughly. A level tablespoon of ground coffee is about 5 g, so the calculator shows a tablespoon amount too. It varies with the grind, so a scale is better if you have one.

Is anything saved?

No. The calculator runs in your browser and nothing is saved or sent anywhere.
